fixture.issue: Issue: the spec producer's Scenarios section can optionally withhold a scenario from the builder for the code-blind evaluator, by marking it holdout (a `holdout` fence-info string on a Given/When/Then block, or a `holdout:` bullet prefix). Explore findings: the marker is recognised only inside `## Scenarios`; selection is producer judgement at spec-write time, bounded by a minority-subset rule (never more than half, never all — the builder must keep at least one visible scenario) and a generalisation rule (a holdout must verify behaviour the WHY/WHAT/HOW body already requires, never be the sole statement of a requirement).

question: Write the `## Scenarios` section of a lite-nlspec for this feature, applying the holdout-selection rules yourself: mark a minority of the scenarios holdout (never all), and make sure every holdout scenario verifies behaviour already stated in the spec body rather than introducing a new, undisclosed requirement.

must_avoid: a new requirement only stated in the holdout
the only place this is required
not mentioned elsewhere in the spec
